subject: MedSage integration recap — embeddings, rerank, streaming funcalls
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <cpark@medsage.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@medsage.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: MedSage integration recap — embeddings, rerank, streaming funcalls

Thanks again for taking the call today — really helpful discussion. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, proposed next steps, and open questions so we can align the pilot scope. Happy to adjust if I missed anything.

Summary of pain / goals (your words):
- Search results have noisy relevance for patient records and clinical notes; current embed + BM25 pipeline returns too many false positives.
- Need a low-latency reranking step for top-K so clinicians see higher precision in the first 1–3 results.
- Real-time triage use case requires streaming responses (partial suggestions) and function-calls to populate structured triage objects into MedSage workflow.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence + IP/network isolation are required for pilot procurement.

What Redwood proposes for pilot scope (initial):
1) Embeddings + rerank prototype: integrate Redwood embeddings -> candidate generation (existing infra) -> online reranker (lightweight model) served via Redwood streaming endpoint.
2) Streaming + function-calls: enable client to receive token-level streaming while triggering a function-call when a structured triage object is confident (we’ll provide example schema).
3) Structured outputs: deliver a JSON schema for triage/follow-up fields (priority, recommended action codes, confidence score).
4) Operational SLOs: target p95 latency for rerank step under 250ms for top-K=10; initial QPS estimate 5–20 depending on button/traffic.

Technical asks from your side:
- Sandbox data sample (10–20 representative queries) and expected gold labels for rerank evaluation.
- Network/egress requirements and whether you prefer Dedicated or Private (VPC) for pilot.
- Any must-have fields in the triage JSON schema.

Immediate next steps / timeline:
- I’ll share a draft Mutual Action Plan (attached) with milestones for a 6-week pilot (tech sync, data delivery, pilot run, evaluation). (Attachment: MS-2027-042_MAP_Draft_20270209.pdf)
- Ben will propose an implementation checklist (SDK changes and sample code) by Thu 2/11.
- MedSage to share the sample queries and security contact for SOC2 documents and procurement path by Fri 2/12.

Open questions we called out:
- Would MedSage prefer streaming tokens first and then send the function-call result, or do you want the server to delay streaming until the function-call completes? Performance tradeoffs vary.
- For rerank model, is there a preference for a lightweight sparse+embed hybrid or pure dense reranker?

Thanks — attaching a short SOC2 summary for quick review (Redwood_SOC2_Summary_20270115.pdf).

Best,
Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_Summary_20270115.pdf

From: Claire Park <cpark@medsage.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@medsage.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:17:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MedSage integration recap — embeddings, rerank, streaming funcalls

Thanks, Irene — this matches what we discussed. Quick clarifications and a couple requests from our side: 

Clarifications:
- We prefer the server to stream partial suggestions immediately; the function-call should trigger when the model detects a structured triage outcome with >=0.85 confidence. Streaming for clinicians is critical for UX.
- For the reranker, the team favors a dense-first approach (dense embeddings + small MLP reranker) because our label set is small but semantic similarity matters.

Requests / procurement notes:
- Procurement wants a short statement of intent that lists pilot deliverables and termination conditions to attach to the SOW. Can Redwood provide a 1-paragraph summary?
- Security will send a short questionnaire and a contact (Tom included). Expect that by EOD Thu.

We’ll aim to deliver the sample queries by Fri 2/12. Also looping in procurement at procurement@medsage.com — they may follow up with PO cadence questions.

Cheers,
Claire Park
Head of Product | MedSage Health

Subject: Re: MedSage integration recap — embeddings, rerank, streaming funcalls

Claire / team — quick implementation notes and SDK changes we’ll deliver in the MAP milestone 1: 

1) SDK + client changes (PR targets):
- New streaming client helper that yields partial messages and an event when a function-call is emitted. We’ll provide an example in Node and Python.
- Rerank helper that accepts candidate IDs + embeddings and calls Redwood rerank endpoint (server-side batching enabled).
- Output validation helper: JSON Schema draft for triage object + a companion validator so you can enforce required fields on ingest.

2) Runtime knobs and default SLOs:
- Default continuous batching window 10ms for low-latency; configurable if you need tighter p99.
- KV cache support for repeated context across clinician sessions (saves token costs).

3) Minimal estimator for pilot cost (rough):
- Embedding units + rerank per 1k requests -> ~0.9 compute unit estimate per 1k; pilot expected around 10k tokens/day initially. We’ll refine once we get sample traffic.

I’m attaching the implementation checklist and will open a PR with sample code by end of day. If MedSage is good with server-first streaming + immediate function-calls on threshold as Claire suggested, we’ll wire the streaming event hook by next week.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
